title: Spouse Visa UK | Partner & Fiancé Visas | Manchester
description: Spouse visa, partner, fiancé(e) and unmarried partner visas explained. IAA-regulated advice in Manchester on the £29,000 requirement and evidence.
intro: If your husband, wife, civil partner, fiancé or long-term partner is British or settled in the UK, a partner visa lets you live here together. We help you choose the right route, meet the financial requirement and put together strong relationship evidence. Whichever spouse visa or partner route fits your relationship, we prepare the application with you.

faqs.q: Can civil partners apply on the same route?
faqs.a: Yes. Civil partners apply on the same partner route as married couples, with the same requirements.

faqs.q: What is the most common reason partner visas are refused?
faqs.a: Missing or incorrect financial evidence. The Home Office is strict about which documents count and which dates they must cover, so we check this carefully before you apply.

faqs.q: Can we apply if my partner is on a Skilled Worker visa?
faqs.a: Not as a spouse under the family route. Partners of Skilled Workers usually apply as dependants on the Skilled Worker route instead. The rules and costs are different, so ask us which applies.

faqs.q: What if we don’t meet the £29,000 requirement?
faqs.a: You may be able to combine income with savings, use different income sources, or qualify under exemptions for some benefits. In some cases there are exceptional circumstances. We look at your full picture at a consultation.

sections.heading: Partner visas: which one fits your relationship?
sections.text:
The UK has several family routes for couples, all under Appendix FM of the Immigration Rules:
- Spouse or civil partner visa: if you are married or in a civil partnership
- Unmarried partner visa: if you have lived together in a relationship like marriage for at least 2 years
- Fiancé(e) or proposed civil partner visa: if you plan to marry in the UK within 6 months of arriving
- Spouse visa extension: to extend after your first 2 years and 6 months or 2 years and 9 months

Your UK partner must be British, Irish, settled in the UK, or have refugee or humanitarian protection.

sections.heading: The requirements every couple must meet
sections.text:
Whichever route you use, the Home Office checks the same main areas:
- Financial requirement: £29,000 a year for most new applications, through income, savings or both
- Genuine relationship: evidence that your relationship is real and continuing
- English language: A1 for a first application, A2 when you extend, and B1 for settlement
- Accommodation: suitable housing in the UK without public funds

Most refusals come from evidence that doesn't meet the strict format the Home Office requires, rather than from couples who don't qualify.

sections.heading: From partner visa to settlement
sections.text: Partner visas usually lead to Indefinite Leave to Remain after 5 years, in two stages of around 2 years and 6 months each. The government's settlement proposals indicate that partners of British citizens would keep a 5-year route, but the final rules haven't been published yet.
